items.title: The 2-inverted Witt sheaf of a Z[1/2]-scheme is the pushforward of the Witt sheaf of its characteristic-zero fibre
items.author: Frédéric Déglise; Jean Fasel; Fangzhou Jin; Adeel A. Khan
items.work: On the rational motivic homotopy category
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.153
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is Proposition 13.2 at source lines 2513-2519, label prop:Witt_2inverted: for a Z[1/2]-scheme S and a subring Lambda of Q with 2 invertible, the canonical map from the Lambda-linear Witt sheaf of S to the pushforward of the Lambda-linear Witt sheaf of the characteristic-zero fibre is an isomorphism. The proof at source lines 2520-2568 is the Witt analogue of the paper's key lemma but is proved directly and not deduced from it: it reduces to regular S and to the map on Witt groups W(S)[1/2] to W(S_Q)[1/2], then uses Balmer's Witt groups with support and the long exact localization sequence of a closed pair to reduce the claim to the vanishing of W^i(S,S_p)[1/2] for every odd prime p, and finally writes down the niveau/Gersten-Witt spectral sequence of W^{-i-j}(S,S_p) whose E^1 terms purity identifies with W(kappa(x)) when i+j is 0 mod 4 and with 0 otherwise. The non-routine step is the last one: those surviving E^1 terms are 2-primary torsion precisely because the residue fields have positive characteristic, so inverting 2 collapses the spectral sequence, and it is this observation, not the machinery itself, that decides the proposition. The argument is a self-contained appendix computation in which each tool is standard but the order and the reduction are specific, so the card is rated H2.
